messages.subject: Plot multiple columns
parts:
Hi list,

I am using ggplot2 to plot the output of an ecological model

I defined a 'base' object that contins basic layout info

base <- ggplot(ep,aes(x=Ur,shape=factor(Ar),linetype=factor(Ar))) + facet_grid(Ae~Av)

then I do the individual plot this way (which works great)

base + geom_line(aes(y=vPop)) + geom_point(aes(y=vPop))
base + geom_line(aes(y=ePop)) + geom_point(aes(y=ePop))

Now let's assume that I want the 'ePop' and 'vPop' variables in the same graph, with different colors (both are columns of the 'ep' dataframe)

How can I do this? I tried to do something like

geom_point(aes(y=ePop),colour=2)

but it add a red overlay to the already existing legend

Is there a way to specify things to have a separate legend for colours?

thanks
t

messages.subject: Re: Plot multiple columns
parts:
Hi:

Perhaps something like this for an individual panel?

df <- data.frame(x = rep(1:10, 2), gp = factor(rep(c('A', 'B'), each = 10)),
                 y1 = rnorm(20), y2 = rnorm(20, 4))
df2 <- melt(df, measure = c('y1', 'y2'))
h <- ggplot(df2, aes(x = x, y = value, shape = gp, linetype = gp,
                     colour = variable))
h + geom_point(size = 3) + geom_line(size = 1) +
  scale_colour_discrete('Response') + scale_shape_discrete('Group') +
  scale_linetype_discrete('Group')

It's easier if you stack the responses into a single variable with melt()
and let it create a factor called variable to hold the response names
prior to generating any code for the graph per se. The values of y1
and y2 are in the variable named value.

In ggplot(), associate variable with colour. It's a lot easier to do it
this way than to massage it inside of the ggplot2 code and define
new scales by hand. It's even better if you name the variables
in your data frame the way you want them titled in the legend; ditto for
the values. Basically, you work harder to massage the data so that you
can use simple ggplot() code to produce a beautiful graph.

I added the scale_* calls just to change the headings...and to illustrate a
point. Had I named the variables in the input data frame according to the
scale headings in the above graph , they would have showed
up automatically. Notice how I needed to change both the shape and
linetype scales to give the same title, since both aesthetics were mapped
to the same variable.

Compare the above code to this:

df3 <- df2    # Copy the melted data frame
names(df3)[2:3] <- c('Group', 'Response')    # Rename gp and variable

# Modify the ggplot call:
h2 <- ggplot(df3, aes(x = x, y = value, shape = Group, linetype = Group,
                       colour = Response))
h2 + geom_point(size = 3) + geom_line(size = 1)

The plot is the same as above, but the call is much cleaner because the
details were handled at the data frame level. Hadley has been harping on
this for the past few weeks, so I thought I'd give a concrete example to
get the point across.


HTH,
Dennis
